title: Confirm proposed interaction and scheduling policies
description: Review docs/PRODUCT.md and docs/DATA-MODEL.md with the user. Confirm four-stream progression/looping/carry-over, MCheyne start date and leap-day policy, published versus working revisions, autosave cadence, trash/export behavior, and working name. Preserve confirmed requirements without reopening them.
acceptance_criteria: Record accepted defaults and unresolved alternatives in decision records; do not claim user approval prematurely.
close_reason: Resolved delegated implementation defaults in docs/decisions/0002-release-defaults.md; Astra reviewed calendar enrollment and undo clarifications. Policies explicitly distinguished from individually user-confirmed preferences and implementation status.

title: Implement read-only migration from the original application
description: Inventory legacy flat/nested Markdown and state snapshot, preserve raw sources/unknown metadata, two-pass links, idempotent import ledger and dry-run report. Do not copy destructive migrateEntries or import absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria: Repeat/interrupted imports retain counts and IDs; CRLF/quoted/date-only/malformed inputs and duplicate filenames are handled; originals byte-identical; unsupported source history reported honestly.

title: Validate complete experience and package Linux and macOS release
description: Integrate all modules; test real SQLite/file failures and real desktop behavior; establish signing/distribution decision and reproducible release artifacts. New app uses separate application identifier/data directory from legacy app.
acceptance_criteria: Both devices pass reading/journaling/export/backup/migration acceptance; all required checks pass; release notes state no sync; rollback preserves original app and source journals.

title: Verify translation sources and offline permissions
description: Investigate official provider availability, edition identity, attribution, offline download and distribution terms for LSB, NASB1995, ESV and KJV. Existing API access is not sufficient evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Document primary sources and source-to-app edition mapping; use synthetic text fixtures until approved content handling is established.
notes: Primary-source findings recorded in docs/TRANSLATION-SOURCES.md on feature/first-desktop-slice. Research establishes KJV live source; full offline rights for LSB/NASB1995/ESV not established. Follow-up task owns source resolution. No external communications.
close_reason: Source and edition matrix documented; unresolved full offline permissions explicitly tracked separately

title: Prove native shell editor and SQLite persistence on both desktops
description: Evaluate proposed Tauri React Rust SQLite boundary and editor candidates before implementation. Use a separate worktree. Prove transactional saves, crash recovery, backup support, Markdown/link round trips, IME, and packaged app startup on Linux and Apple Silicon.
acceptance_criteria: Record selected bindings/editor and measured evidence on both platforms; distinguish CI compilation from actual native smoke tests. No sync service or unrestricted webview SQL.
notes: Beginning a reversible first runnable slice under sj-kfw at user request to continue the app. Proposed technology/interaction choices remain documented; full spike acceptance still requires both Linux and macOS evidence.

comments.author: Ernest Chuang
comments.text: Access assessment from sj-kfw audit: no Apple-Silicon Mac is reachable from the current x86_64 Linux worker. There is no local macOS toolchain, SSH has no named host, and the repository has zero self-hosted GitHub runners. GitHub-hosted macos-latest CI compiles/tests only and its job metadata exposes no Apple-Silicon hardware label; it cannot establish native WebKit runtime behavior. When the intended M2/Apple-Silicon Mac is accessible, use an isolated synthetic-data native smoke, adapt the Linux Hyprland/AT-SPI automation to macOS-native controls, and record runtime, close/restart, SQLite recovery, IME and packaged-startup evidence separately from CI.

title: Implement journal revisions drafts and internal relationships
description: Implement docs/DATA-MODEL.md invariants, immutable complete snapshots, working/published heads, revision generation concurrency, stable links/backlinks, search, trash and explicit purge.
acceptance_criteria: Every persisted autosave is retained under agreed policy; crash/out-of-order/restore/link-rename tests pass; rebuilding derived queries preserves results.
notes: Final design review adds atomic Finish semantics: flush exact pending editor generation and publish it in the same transaction; reject stale finish requests. Every persisted autosave is retained.

comments.author: Ernest Chuang

Stale-writer recovery and maximum dirty interval tracked sj-xfr.

title: Implement offline scripture and unrestricted continuous reader
description: Implement structured passage references, four translations, validated resumable offline downloads and chapter-window reader with anchor preservation. Plan selection must not bound scrolling.
acceptance_criteria: Scroll backward/forward across books including short chapters; preserve anchor on switch/resize; cancellation never reports download success; failed persistence is visible.

acceptance_criteria: Apply agreed progression policies; changing plan definitions preserves completed assignments; streams advance independently; no scrolling-based completion.

Enrollment, completion/undo history, built-in datasets, Tauri commands, and UI remain follow-up work.
notes:
Implementation branch feature/sj-5nz-6-plan-core from integration commit 64127a5. Owns crates/journal-core only.
Implemented schema-v2 plan definition persistence in crates/journal-core. Contract: schemaVersion 1 definitions use a strict tagged schedule union (explicitSchedule or chapterStreams), canonical 1-66 book/chapter references, immutable retained version rows, generated stable plan/version UUIDs, and consecutive per-plan version numbers. Existing schema-v1 journal rows migrate transactionally without modification. Validation passed: cargo test (30 tests), cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, git diff --check. Tests now reject John 3:999-1000 without adding a partial version, accept the John 3:36 boundary, and verify the next valid version remains ordinal 2. The schema-v1 upgrade fixture now preserves two entries, a stable link, and three retained revisions across migration. Revalidated 30 tests, Clippy warnings denied, formatting, diff check, and exact 1,189-count source comparison. Awaiting renewed root/Astra review.

title: Refuse coincidental legacy occurrence realignment after divergent history
description: Independent review of c1f18fe found migrate_assignment_positions in crates/journal-core/src/plans.rs (lines 404-425) validates each assignment independently and resumes assigning occurrence positions after a contradictory earlier snapshot. Reproduction with real SQLite: define stop stream Genesis [1,2,1,3,1,4], start at 0, retain legacy first-match history [1,2,1,2,1] with ordinal 5 active and all cycles 1. Migration leaves ordinal 4 null but assigns ordinal 5 position 4; complete_plan_stream succeeds and creates ordinal 6 chapter 4. Chapter 3 was never assigned/read. A temporary integration probe review_legacy_divergence_must_not_realign_by_coincidence failed its expected-refusal assertion and showed Some(4) followed by Some(5)/chapter 4. Probe removed; review commit contains bookkeeping only. Fixture can be built with five v5 assignments, drop immutability and position-required triggers, change ordinal 4 passage chapter to 2, drop stream_position, recreate immutability trigger, set user_version=4 and reopen.
acceptance_criteria: Validate reconstructed occurrence history as a coherent prefix: after the first contradiction, later coincidental passage matches must not authorize guessed continuation. Preserve every assignment/completion/undo/epoch and passage snapshot. Add a durable regression for [1,2,1,3,1,4] with legacy [1,2,1,2,1], assert deliberate refusal and exact unchanged rows after attempted completion, plus reopen and ordered undo/recompletion behavior. Consider databases already migrated to v5 by c1f18fe so the repair cannot leave unsafe assigned suffix positions usable. Run full journal-core tests, rustfmt, Clippy; request independent review.
notes: Implementation checkpoint 2026-09-18: schema v6 audits assignment occurrence metadata as one coherent prefix. For v4 rows it derives the documented legacy first-match start; for v5 rows it preserves the explicit retained start. Ordinals must be consecutive and every cycle, passage snapshot, and existing position must match. At the first contradiction, that assignment and the entire suffix receive null derived positions, so later coincidental chapter matches cannot authorize skipped progression. The v6 repair also runs on already-migrated v5 databases. Assignments, passage snapshots, completions, undos and epochs remain retained; only unsafe derived position metadata is cleared. Regression reproduces definition [1,2,1,3,1,4] with retained [1,2,1,2,1], includes undo/recompletion history, proves ordinal 5 refuses completion after reopen, fingerprints retained records before/after the rejected request, and proves ordered undo exposes the divergent row while recompletion of the coherent prefix rolls back against retained conflicting history. Validation: 39 Rust tests pass, rustfmt passes, Clippy all targets passes with warnings denied, git diff check passes. Keep in_progress pending independent migration/data-integrity re-review.
close_reason: Independent review approved 23451a0; coherent-prefix v4/v5 repair and transactional refusal verified; all 39 tests and static checks pass.

title: Investigate intermittent retained enrollment occurrence reset
description: Independent review at 5a2fc85: first npm test failed src/plans/PlanPanel.test.tsx:446, test enrolls the exact selected retained version once with explicit occurrence and loop choices. Expected repeat stream startingPosition 1 but actual enrollInChapterStreams payload was 0; short stream loopAfterEnd false was preserved. 138/139 passed; immediate full rerun passed 139/139 and build. No production or test edits. Inspect async initial discovery and retained choice initialization useEffect at PlanPanel.tsx:144-151 plus handlers at :641; controls render with fallback defaults before choice state is initialized, which is a candidate timing window, not a confirmed root cause. Reproduce deterministically using deferred discovery/effect timing; determine test synchronization versus real interactive reset. Preserve explicit occurrence/loop choices in exact submitted payload and add durable regression without merely retrying or weakening assertions. Request independent review after fix.
acceptance_criteria: Explain and deterministically cover the observed 1-to-0 payload mismatch; preserve user input through initial discovery/selection; full frontend tests and build pass; independent review required.
notes: Root cause confirmed: retained chapter-stream controls rendered fallback defaults before a passive initialization effect populated retainedEnrollmentChoices. An input event in that window mapped the empty array, silently discarded startingPosition 1, and the later effect installed position 0. Fixed by deriving complete default choices synchronously for render and submission, materializing the complete stream choice set on the first input update, and removing the passive initializer/reset race. Added a deterministic empty-state occurrence transition regression; the existing exact-payload interaction regression still verifies startingPosition 1 and loop choices. Validation: the two occurrence regressions passed 20 consecutive focused runs; full frontend suite passed 140/140; production TypeScript/Vite build and diff check passed. A broader PlanPanel stress loop independently exposed a different intermittent retained-export error/selection failure and is tracked separately; it does not reproduce in the occurrence tests. Ready for independent review; keep parent plan/release milestones open.
close_reason: Occurrence reset fixed in 9ce425f and independently approved by sj-5nz.6.100.1; deterministic regression, 140 frontend tests and build pass.

title: Investigate intermittent retained export selection error loss
description: While stress-running the full PlanPanel test file during sj-5nz.6.100 validation, the existing retained-definition export success/error tests intermittently failed because the expected exported JSON or error never appeared after clicking export. DOM retained a valid selected definition but no result. The normal full suite passed immediately beforehand. Investigate selection/discovery versus retained export epoch timing deterministically; preserve the selected immutable version and visible success/failure/retry state. This is separate from the occurrence-choice fix.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministically reproduce the retained export selection/result race; fix without weakening assertions; add lifecycle regression; frontend tests/build pass; independent review.
notes: Root cause confirmed: discovery committed selectedDefinitionId and rendered the retained export control before the passive [api, selectedDefinitionId] reset effect ran. An export started in that window incremented retainedExportEpoch, then the queued effect incremented it again and cleared/ignored the eventual success or failure. Fixed by making selection changes synchronously invalidate old export state and update selectedDefinitionIdRef before rendering; initial/refresh discovery and user selection all use this transition. The remaining api-only effect handles adapter replacement. Added deferred discovery plus deferred export settlement coverage. Validation: all 74 PlanPanel tests passed 10 consecutive full-file runs; full frontend suite passed 141/141; production TypeScript/Vite build and git diff check passed. Ready for independent review; do not close plan/release milestones.

title: Pin export directory access against concurrent path replacement
description: Safety review of crates/journal-core/src/export.rs: check_components validates destination ancestors once, but subsequent open_regular, NamedTempFile, read_optional, rename, persist, and directory fsync calls resolve paths again. O_NOFOLLOW protects the final component only. Renaming the selected directory or recovery directory and substituting a symlink after validation can redirect later operations outside the selected destination and detach operations from the locked directory. Scope: anchor operations to verified directory handles with safe relative resolution on supported Linux/macOS, or fail safely without touching a substituted destination. Preserve original journal/export data.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic tests swap destination and recovery directories after validation and before read/write/rename; no outside file is created, modified, or moved and no private output escapes. Lock and manifest operations stay associated with the verified directory. Existing symlink, collision, recovery and external-edit tests continue to pass. State supported-platform and residual race limitations.
close_reason: Completed Unix descriptor-relative export migration and directory-substitution regressions, including entry replacement/recovery; platform and residual-race limitations documented. Linux tests/check pass; macOS release validation remains tracked under sj-kfw.
